title: Ingest the full 2026 game log
problem: Only standings are available, so the model cannot adjust for opponent strength or estimate home-field advantage.
a: Scrape nfl.com/schedules/2026/by-week/week-N for N=1..9 and store final scores.
b: Use an official gamebook feed if one is licensed.
c: Do nothing; keep raw net-points ratings.
recommendation: Option A. It is the cheapest path and it unblocks Q-01, Q-10 and Q-11 at once.

title: Replace unofficial depth charts with official participation data
problem: 31 of 32 club charts are self-labelled unofficial, 27 print no date, and Houston publishes only an image. Two clubs contradict their own news pages.
a: Switch the starter flag to official gamebook participation data.
b: Keep club charts but add a staleness diff and a conflict flag on every run.
c: Drop the depth layer entirely and rely only on the injury report.
recommendation: Option A as the target, Option B as the immediate stop-gap. Option C loses the 2nd/3rd/4th-string requirement in R-17.

title: Create a separate, clearly-labelled vendor tier for market lines
problem: The system is meant to beat a market, but no market data exists and no official source publishes it.
a: Add a second dataset tier with its own badge; fact rows stay official-only, vendor rows are marked vendor.
b: Refuse to use any non-official data at all.
c: Mix them into one table with no tier badge.
recommendation: Option A. Option B makes R-09 unachievable. Option C breaks the verification rule in R-04.

title: Surface a fetch timestamp on every ingested row
problem: We cannot currently prove how fresh an injury row or a depth chart was at the moment a signal fired.
a: Store and render an ISO fetch timestamp next to every row.
b: Store the timestamp but only show it on the Flagged page.
recommendation: Option A. It is the only way to audit a losing bet after the fact.

title: Always override the depth chart with the injury report
problem: Detroit lists Cade Mays as starting centre while the official report lists him Out. Philadelphia lists two players the club waived.
a: Make the injury report authoritative for availability and the chart authoritative only for the replacement order.
c: Show both and let the user decide per row.
recommendation: Option A, already implemented. Option B produces known-wrong starters. Option C does not scale to 32 clubs.

title: Add the official inactives list as a final pre-kickoff gate
problem: An 'Out' injury designation is not the same as being on the official inactives list.
a: Ingest the per-week inactives article and treat it as the final override.
recommendation: Option A. Option B will occasionally produce a signal on a player who was never going to play.

title: Publish model output with its parameters visible
problem: A rating with HFA = 0.0 and no schedule adjustment looks like a line but is not one.
a: Render every model output with its parameter set and an explicit 'uncalibrated' badge until Q-10/Q-11 are closed.
b: Suppress model output until it is fully calibrated.
recommendation: Option A. Option B hides progress; Option C is how a bad model gets trusted.

title: Control for multiplicity across the whole strategy book
problem: With many strategies, some will look profitable by chance alone.
a: Use Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at 10% within declared strategy families, and report the effective number of independent tests.
b: Use a plain p < 0.05 per strategy.
recommendation: Option A. Option B manufactures false positives. Option C is defensible but needlessly strict; it is the fallback until Q-15 is closed.

title: Make out-of-sample performance a hard gate, not a report
problem: A strategy tuned on the same data it is scored on is not evidence.
a: Require a pre-registered parameter set, then grade it only on data after the registration date.
b: Allow tuning but penalise the score.
recommendation: Option A. It is the only version of this that actually removes hindsight.

title: Add a market-vig break-even floor to every gate
problem: A strategy that beats nothing but loses less than the vig is still losing.
a: Require the modelled edge to clear the book's margin before a bet is allowed.
b: Ignore vig at the research stage.
c: Use a fixed arbitrary edge threshold.
recommendation: Option A. Option B is fine for research but must not gate capital; Option C is arbitrary.

title: Estimate leg correlations on within-game residuals
problem: Correlating raw totals makes unrelated legs look correlated because they share a game script.
a: De-mean each statistic within game and correlate the residuals.
recommendation: Option A. Option C systematically under-prices parlay variance and is the single most common way a parlay book blows up.

title: Start the leaderboard on notional stakes
problem: Cash rewards create an incentive to game the scoring function.
a: Score in notional units for the first full season; revisit once the gate machinery has a track record.
recommendation: Option A. Option B invites gaming before we know the gates work. Option C removes the incentive the brief asks for.

title: Add a strategy detail page per strategy
problem: The strategy register is dense; each strategy needs its own parameters, gate history and result log.
a: One page per strategy, generated from the register.
b: Keep everything on one page with filters.
recommendation: Option A once any strategy has graded results. Option B is fine while everything is pre-launch.

title: Wire an automated pre-kickoff pipeline run
problem: Injury and depth data change daily; a stale site is a real risk once signals are acted on.
a: Schedule the ingest+build workflow twice daily plus a run before kickoff.
recommendation: Option A. Option B contradicts R-24. Option C is worse than useless for injury data.

title: Auto-file blocked strategies into the Suggestions queue
problem: When a strategy fails its gates nothing currently happens to it.
a: On gate failure, create a suggestion with the failure reason attached so a reviewer picks a path.
recommendation: Option A. It closes the loop between validation and decision-making, which is the point of the Suggestions page.

title: Get a jurisdiction opinion before any real staking
problem: The operating jurisdiction is unspecified, so the applicable rules for originating lines, staking, and rewards are unknown.
a: Legal review before the first real-money bet.
recommendation: Option A, then B while A is pending. Option C is not acceptable.
